I identify one phase: Pr3(ReO5)2 (mp-1209366).

1. **Single-phase fits:** I fitted four candidates one at a time. mp-1209366 gave R = 0.52 at 0 % strain. The other three fitted badly: SiBi2O5 (mp-28144) gave R = 0.99, LiV3O6 (mp-1176549) gave 1.02 and TiMnO3 (mp-19376) gave 1.01. Their residuals still contained the main observed peaks, near 18.8°, 24.7°, 26.6°, 28.6° and 33.9°, at full height.
2. **Residual after mp-1209366:** I don't see any leftover peaks. What remains are up-and-down pairs centred on peaks the model already has, with the largest point at 22 % of the observed maximum. That pattern points to small mismatches in peak position or shape, not a missing phase.
3. **Second-phase tests:** Adding Ba2Pr(CuO2)4 (mp-6779) or Ba2LuCu3O7 (mp-20324) gave each a weight of 0.00 and left R at 0.52.

I did not fit the other four candidates (mp-775462, mp-5777, mp-753482 and mp-6779 alone). I also only tested two of the possible partners for a second phase. Since the residual has no leftover peaks, a second phase seems unlikely, but the remaining partners weren't checked directly.

{"present": ["mp-1209366"], "confidence": 0.85, "note": "Pr3(ReO5)2 alone fits with R = 0.52 and leaves only paired residuals at its own peaks; two added candidates got zero weight, and the other three fits failed with R near 1."}
